title: Xuanzang’s Westward Journey
desc: In the third year of the Zhenguan reign, Master Xuanzang set out from Chang’an on a seventeen-year journey west to India to seek the Dharma, covering fifty thousand li and laying the historical foundation for the later scripture-fetching story.

title: Great Tang Records on the Western Regions
desc: After Xuanzang returned to the Tang, he dictated his travels; the monk Bianji transcribed them into the twelve-volume Great Tang Records on the Western Regions, recording the customs of over a hundred lands and becoming the documentary basis of the scripture-fetching narrative.

title: The Poetic Tale of Fetching Scriptures
desc: The Southern Song publication The Poetic Tale of the Tang Monk’s Scripture Fetching is the earliest surviving literary version of the journey; the Monkey Pilgrim appears for the first time, forming the prototype of the pilgrimage troupe.

title: Zaju Play Journey to the West
desc: Yang Jingxian’s Yuan zaju play Journey to the West, in six books and twenty-four acts, solidified the image of Sun Wukong and completed the cast of Sha Wujing and Zhu Bajie, bringing the narrative close to completion.

title: Finalized Shidetang Edition
desc: In the twentieth year of the Wanli reign (1592), the hundred-chapter Shidetang edition of Journey to the West was published in Jinling; credited to the Master of the Huayang Cavern, it marked the final standardization of the hundred-chapter novel form.

title: Zhengdao Commentary (Journey to the West)
desc: Wang Xiangxu’s early-Qing commentary Zhengdao Shu interpreted Journey to the West through Daoist inner alchemy, pioneering Qing commentary and placing the novel within the neidan (inner alchemy) exegetical tradition.

title: Modern Collated Edition
desc: The People’s Literature Publishing House issued Huang Suqiu’s collated and annotated edition, based on the Shidetang text and collated against various Ming and Qing editions, becoming the standard modern text.

title: Shidetang Hundred-Chapter Edition
desc: The Wanli-era Jinling Shidetang imprint in twenty volumes and one hundred chapters is the earliest surviving hundred-chapter edition, the ancestor of all later versions, now held in the Tenri Central Library in Japan.

title: Zhengdao Edition
desc: Wang Xiangxu’s annotated edition of the second year of Kangxi (1663) abridged the Shidetang text and added inner-alchemy commentary, initiating the line of abridged-and-commented Qing editions.

title: True Interpretation of Journey to the West
desc: Chen Shibin’s one-hundred-chapter True Interpretation of Journey to the West (1718) drew on both Chan Buddhism and inner alchemy for mutual corroboration, becoming one of the most popular Qing commentaries.

title: Yadong Typeset Edition
desc: Wang Yuanfang of the Yadong Library punctuated and typeset Journey to the West, pioneering modern punctuation and advancing the modern reading of classical novels.

title: People’s Literature Collated Edition
desc: Huang Suqiu’s collated edition for the People’s Literature Publishing House, based on the Shidetang text and collated against other versions, served as the standard edition for half a century.

title: New Annotated Edition
desc: Huang Suqiu’s new collated and annotated edition for the People’s Literature Publishing House was revised and reprinted with expanded notes and collation records, becoming more scholarly.

title: Digital Edition
desc: A digital full-text search and multi-version collation system for classical texts went online, enabling side-by-side comparison of the Shidetang, Zhengdao, and True Interpretation editions.

title: Ming Dynasty Opera Adaptations
desc: Ming folk opera dramatized the Journey to the West story; both court and popular troupes staged Mulian and scripture-fetching plays, marking the beginning of the story’s operatic adaptation.

title: Qing Dynasty New Year Prints
desc: New Year print workshops in Yangliuqing, Wuqiang, and elsewhere mass-produced Journey to the West prints, bringing the Monkey King and scripture-fetching imagery into popular festive visual culture.

title: Popularization of Lianhuanhua Comics
desc: The Shanghai World Book Company published the picture-book Journey to the West, carrying the story at scale into the reading of children and city dwellers.

title: Princess Iron Fan Animation
desc: The Wan brothers’ Princess Iron Fan, China’s first animated feature film, premiered; a pioneer of Asian animation, it brought the Journey to the West to the screen.

title: CCTV Journey to the West
desc: The CCTV television series Journey to the West, starring Liu Xiao Ling Tong, was rebroadcast over a thousand times across its twenty-five episodes, becoming a national visual memory of the story.

title: A Chinese Odyssey
desc: Stephen Chow’s two-part A Chinese Odyssey premiered, deconstructing Journey to the West in a postmodern mode and becoming a subcultural classic of the internet age.

title: Journey to the West: Conquering the Demons
desc: Stephen Chow’s Journey to the West: Conquering the Demons topped the Spring Festival box office, relaunching the Journey to the West blockbuster franchise.

title: Games and Web Fiction
desc: The Black Myth: Wukong trailer went viral worldwide; Journey to the West web fiction and cross-media adaptations continue to be produced, regenerating the franchise.
